provider.name: Encyclopedia of Life
provider.organization_type: global species knowledge, taxonomy, media, descriptive content, traits, collections, and data integration platform
provider.description: Encyclopedia of Life aggregates and organizes species knowledge from many providers, including scientific and common names, taxonomic hierarchies, descriptions, media, maps, references, collections, communities, and structured trait data through TraitBank.
institutional_context: Encyclopedia of Life project and partner institutions
Natural history museums, taxonomic databases, and research organizations

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting EOL documentation, taxon-page and hierarchy guidance, content and media metadata, TraitBank documentation, collections, communities, curation, content-partner feeds, APIs, downloads, licenses, citations, and organizational context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: EOL and its contributing providers remain authoritative for page associations, content provenance, trait records, media, licenses, APIs, terms, citation, and contact information.

notes: Verify whether legacy versioned EOL API endpoints remain supported and whether newer services supersede them.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, or account credentials in this manifest.
Capture parameters, response fields, pagination, licenses, errors, deprecations, and rate limits.
Distinguish API responses from bulk exports, TraitBank downloads, and content-partner resource feeds.
Capture exact content-object, trait-record, and provider-level license wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate taxonomic facts, descriptive text, images, audio, video, maps, trait records, collections, APIs, and source code.
Preserve rights holder, contributor, source URL, content partner, resource identifier, license URI, and bibliographic citation.
Do not assume EOL aggregation grants broader rights than the original provider license.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some documentation paths, API versions, legacy endpoints, GitHub organizations, or status pages may have moved or been retired; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every taxon page, data object, collection, community, content partner, trait term, or API result when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, account credentials, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Taxonomic facts, text, media, maps, traits, collections, provider feeds, APIs, and source code may carry different rights.
Always preserve EOL page identifiers, provider identifiers, content partner, source URL, rights holder, license, trait predicate, trait object, unit, context, citation, and provenance.
